title: Internal/sectionwise normalization of the scalar-change direct-image unit
statement:
Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings and $f:X\to Y$ any morphism of schemes, with pro-etale sites small in the module universe [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $Z=X,Y$ put $R_Z=p_Z^*R$, $S_Z=p_Z^*S$, and $a_Z=p_Z^*a$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $c_R:f^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X$ and $c_S:f^{-1}S_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}S_X$ be the coefficient isomorphisms $\alpha_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] for $R$ and $S$; as components of one natural isomorphism $f^*p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ they satisfy $a_Xc_R=c_Sf^{-1}a_Y$. Assume extension of scalars $S_Z\otimes_{R_Z}-$ is exact. Let $\mathcal E_{R,Z}$ and $\mathcal E_{S,Z}$ be the termwise derived equivalences from internal ring-object modules to modules over their reconstructed section-ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Internally and sectionwise put $L_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$, let $U_Z$ be exact scalar restriction, and denote the scalar unit by $\eta^Z$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the specified geometric adjunctions $Lf_R^*\dashv Rf_{*,R}$, $Lf_S^*\dashv Rf_{*,S}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every internal $C\in D(R_X)$ define
$$\beta_C:L_YRf_{*,R}C\longrightarrow Rf_{*,S}L_XC$$
as the $S$-geometric adjunct of
$$Lf_S^*L_YRf_{*,R}C\xrightarrow{\sim}L_XLf_R^*Rf_{*,R}C\xrightarrow{L_X(\epsilon_C)}L_XC,$$
where $\epsilon$ is the $R$-geometric counit and the first map is the canonical pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
Under the canonical derived operation, scalar-adjunction and tensor comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization, lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction, lem-pd-section-derived-tensor-normalization], $\mathcal E_{S,Y}(\beta_C)$ equals the section-ring map defined by this same counit formula. For this section-ring map use the specified adjunction-compatible isomorphism $d:U_YRf_{*,S}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,R}U_X$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] for $u=f$, the section-ring maps of $a_X,a_Y$ and of $c_R,c_S$, and write $\bar C=\mathcal E_{R,X}C$. With $M=Rf_{*,R}\bar C$ the map $t=d_{L_X\bar C}\circ U_Y(\beta_{\bar C})$ satisfies the equality in $D(R_Y)$
$$t\circ\eta^Y_M=Rf_{*,R}(\eta^X_{\bar C}).$$
These comparisons preserve the coefficient actions: if an integer $s$ is invertible in $S$, then $t$ intertwines inverse multiplication by $s$ on its source and $Rf_{*,R}$ of inverse multiplication by $s$ on $U_XL_X\bar C$. No boundedness, quasi-compactness, properness, constructibility or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\theta:Lf_S^*L_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}L_XLf_R^*$ for the pullback/scalar comparison in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] to $a:R\to S$: its comparison $\lambda$ is $\theta$, using the canonical symmetry to write scalar extension with $S$ on the left. Its formula is $f^{-1}(s\otimes m)\mapsto c_S(f^{-1}s)\otimes f^{-1}m$, with the $R$ action identified by $c_R$. This is the balanced pullback/tensor comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism. The coefficient square $a_Xc_R=c_Sf^{-1}a_Y$ is precisely what makes that formula balanced. That node identifies this actual map with the section-ring construction. In addition [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] identifies the geometric adjunctions, including their counits; [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] identifies scalar extension, restriction and their specified adjunctions; and [lem-pd-section-derived-tensor-normalization] identifies the actual tensor/pullback arrow and its unit constraints. All hypotheses hold on the small pro-etale sites of the statement, with their sheaf tensor. Thus these are the specified comparisons appearing in the question.

proof.text: For an internal $C$, its defining adjunct is $q_C=L_X(\epsilon_C)\circ\theta_{Rf_{*,R}C}$. The comparisons of step 1 send this composite to $L_X(\epsilon_{\bar C})\circ\theta_{Rf_{*,R}\bar C}$: they preserve composition, identify $L_X$ and $Rf_*$, send $\epsilon_C$ to the specified section counit, and send $\theta$ to the specified section comparison. They identify the Hom bijections of the geometric adjunctions. Consequently the image of $\beta_C$ and the section-ring map defined in the question have the same adjunct. Injectivity of that Hom bijection proves their equality, which proves the first assertion. From now on work sectionwise and write $F=Lf_R^*$, $G=Rf_{*,R}$, $H=Lf_S^*$, $J=Rf_{*,S}$, $C=\bar C$, and $M=GC$, with $\epsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$. Thus $q=L_X(\epsilon_C)\circ\theta_M:HL_YM\to L_XC$ and its $H\dashv J$ adjunct is $\beta_C$.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); injectivity of the specified Hom bijection, using step 1

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $u=f$, the section-ring maps $a_X,a_Y$, and the specified $c_R,c_S$. Its hypotheses are exactly the coefficient isomorphisms and the commuting square in the statement, so it supplies $b:U_XH\xrightarrow{\sim}FU_Y$ and the stipulated $d:U_YJ\xrightarrow{\sim}GU_X$, with their stated adjunction compatibility. In particular the $F\dashv G$ adjunct of
$$U_X(q)\circ b_{L_YM}^{-1}:FU_YL_YM\longrightarrow U_XL_XC$$
is $d_{L_XC}\circ U_Y(\beta_C)=t$. Naturality of the Hom bijection in its source then makes the adjunct of $t\circ\eta^Y_M$ equal to
$$U_X(q)\circ b_{L_YM}^{-1}\circ F(\eta^Y_M).$$
Here the direction of $b^{-1}$ is essential: its domain is $FU_YL_YM$.

For every $A\in D(R_Y)$ the normalized comparisons satisfy
$$(U_X\theta_A)\circ b_{L_YA}^{-1}\circ F(\eta^Y_A)=\eta^X_{FA}.$$
The geometric module pullbacks are exact by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] computes them termwise on every complex, including $U_YL_Y P$; exact scalar extension is assumed. To check this equality, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to A$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its geometric pullback is flat-term K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and computes $FA$. The ordinary scalar squares and Hom transposes required by [lem-sfb-derived-section-scalar-transport] are furnished by [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]; the transport statement gives the derived unit from the ordinary chain unit. The latter node fixes that unit as $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. On these representatives [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] fixes $\theta$ by the pure-tensor formula of step 1, while [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] fixes $b$ by identified-coefficient inverse image. Thus the left side sends a generalized inverse-image element $f^{-1}m$ first to $f^{-1}(1\otimes m)$ and then to $1\otimes f^{-1}m$, exactly the right side. This is an equality of maps of inverse-image module sheaves, checked before the sheafification and balancing universal maps, not a test at geometric points. It holds in each degree and commutes with differentials. Localizing and using the resolution comparisons gives the displayed equality for $A$.

proof.text:
Substitute $q=L_X(\epsilon_C)\circ\theta_M$ into the last formula of step 3 and use step 4 with $A=M=GC$. The $F\dashv G$ adjunct of $t\circ\eta^Y_M$ is
$$U_XL_X(\epsilon_C)\circ U_X(\theta_M)\circ b_{L_YM}^{-1}\circ F(\eta^Y_M)
=U_XL_X(\epsilon_C)\circ\eta^X_{FM}
=\eta^X_C\circ\epsilon_C.$$
The second equality is naturality of the scalar unit for the morphism $\epsilon_C:FM\to C$. On the other hand the adjunct of $G(\eta^X_C):GC\to GU_XL_XC$ is
$$\epsilon_{U_XL_XC}\circ FG(\eta^X_C)=\eta^X_C\circ\epsilon_C,$$
by naturality of the geometric counit. Therefore the two maps have equal adjuncts. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives $t\circ\eta^Y_M=G(\eta^X_C)$, as required. These are only naturality and composition identities for the adjunctions already fixed in steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: Finally let $s\in\mathbf Z$ be invertible in $S$. Its inverse pulls to $S_X,S_Y$, so multiplication by $s$ is an automorphism of $L_YM$ and $L_XC$, with inverse multiplication by $s^{-1}$. Put $A_0=U_YL_YM$, $B_0=GU_XL_XC$, $v=[s^{-1}]_{A_0}$ and $w=G([s^{-1}]_{U_XL_XC})$. All the equivalences and functors used to form the comparisons are additive, as are scalar restriction and the derived module direct image (the latter applies the additive ordinary direct image to K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]). Thus $v$ inverts $[s]_{A_0}$, and $w$ inverts $[s]_{B_0}=G([s]_{U_XL_XC})$. Every morphism of the additive derived category commutes with integer multiplication, so $t[s]_{A_0}=[s]_{B_0}t$. Multiplying by these two inverses gives $tv=wt$. This is the asserted inverse-multiplication compatibility. Additive comparison equivalences preserve $[s]$ and its unique inverse as well. The argument used no boundedness, finiteness, constructibility, completeness or geometric condition on $f$.
